Author API decided. Jack Heart, asked "A (one server you write) or B (play and agent functions)": "b is fine". Build B and release the hold. The author writes play(match, agents) -> Tables (the game, in a light module, no Torch) and load(player, config) -> Agent, where Agent.act(rows) answers one batch and must answer each row as if alone (each row carries its own seed). EvalJob(name/tournament, checkpoints, play=play, agents=Agents(load=load, config=...)); with no agents=, play(match) does everything itself through the same Etude-run game processes. Etude owns: light game processes importing only play's module; one agent process per machine holding loaded agents (least recently used dropped by bytes), batching requests per player key by max batch and max delay (reasonable defaults); direct transport from game processes to the agent process, never a relay through a parent; deadlines; failed+retry (agent process exit = retry=true for in-flight matches; a load that raises = that player's matches failed retry=false, run failed, never recorded succeeded); per-match delivery; how many games are active (CPUs, capped by memory the agent config states). Observations and actions must be picklable values (NumPy arrays, plain values). Delete InferenceServer, serve-handle, play(match, inference), server=, EvalJob.workers. "Policy" is reserved for PolicyKey (EXP-75): call the loaded object Agent. Performance bar is the 28-worker scalar CPU baseline; unproven without a rental, say so in the PR. EXP-66 PR #113 is merging; sync onto main once it has merged.
